name: Durango bombing – Santa María de Uribarri
story: On 31 March 1937, the first day of General Mola's offensive against Biscay, Italian Savoia-Marchetti S.81 bombers with German and Italian escorts attacked Durango, a road and rail junction behind the front. The first wave struck at about 8 a.m., during morning Mass. The Jesuit church and the Santa Susana convent were hit and priests, nuns and worshippers were killed; Santa María de Uribarri was also damaged. Further raids followed that day. Durango was bombed almost four weeks before Gernika and is often called its forgotten precursor. The town's bombing route links the damaged churches and memorial plaques.
see: The Uribarri basilica with its large wooden porch, plus plaques and panels on the town's bombing route (Bonbardaketaren ibilbidea) marking the sites hit.
plan: Pick up the bombing-route leaflet at the Durango tourist office; the centre is compact and easy to walk in about an hour.

vis.label: Booking
vis.text: Durango tourist office offers the 'Aztarnak' bombing leaflet (downloadable) and an audioguide route; reservations via the office

boxes.text: Deaths are given as about 250 in most accounts; Spanish-language studies give a range of 248–336.
